raw_response:
I am getting old now, so this year I will not spread myself too thin. On my 12 mu, I will keep most land in the usual wheat-maize rotation because that is the safest way for me to hold grain yield and income, and I will keep a smaller piece in cotton because I have grown it many years and it still helps me spread risk. I only have 2 people at home, and I have to think about my strength, not only yield. Wheat and maize are familiar, and with the well I can protect them if spring is dry. Cotton needs more hand work, so I will not plant too much of it.

For wheat, I will stay close to what worked before: sow in early October, use a normal local improved variety, put most fertilizer before sowing and a smaller topdress at jointing. If I cut fertilizer too much, I worry the wheat will turn yellow and lose ears; if I push too much, that is extra cash tied up. So I will use a middle amount, a bit on the safe side. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly on the same 8 mu, with simple tillage so I do not miss the moisture and planting window. Maize I usually do with one main fertilizer dose and one light topdress if the stand looks weak. Cotton I will keep on 4 mu only. It can bring cash, but it takes more labor for management and picking, and at my age that matters a lot. So I will fertilize it moderately and irrigate only when the field is really dry.
